threads.body: [General] Delivery spans can report attributes from the pre-recovery connection. `TracedDelegatingConsumer` snapshots `channel.getConnection()` when the consumer is registered and reuses that `Connection` for every `DeliveryRequest`, so after automatic recovery this extractor reads the old server properties instead of the current inner connection. Retain the channel/current-connection supplier and resolve the connection when each delivery starts; add a delivery-after-recovery assertion as well.

With this change `2.7.0` isn't tested any more. Usually we test the earliest supported version. If some features are not available in the earliest supported version you can use reflection. Alternatively it is possible to compile tests agains newer version but still run tests with the earliest version (test can be disabled via `Assumptions.assumeTrue` when it isn't supported). Newer versions can be tested in a suite.

[General] The PR and #19821 require two independent opt-ins, but this enables both attributes through the existing umbrella `experimental-span-attributes` setting. Users who enabled that setting for the existing RabbitMQ attributes will unexpectedly start emitting vhost/cluster data, and users cannot enable only one of the new attributes. Please read the two new configuration keys independently, gate each `put` with its own flag, and update metadata, documentation, and tests accordingly.

[Style] `rabbitMqContainer` is only accessed by this package-private base class and a same-package subclass, so `protected` exposes it more broadly than needed. Keep it package-private in accordance with least-access visibility.
[Style] This extension is only referenced within `RabbitMqTest`; make it private to use the least necessary visibility, matching the adjacent `testing` extension.

[Testing] Use the existing `experimental(...)` helper for these opt-in expected values instead of repeating the flag ternary; this is the test suite's established mode-dependent assertion convention.

threads.body: This registers the connection attributes on the shared channel builder, so they are emitted for administrative commands (for example `queue.declare` and `exchange.declare`) and settle spans as well as publish spans. That is broader than the PR description's publish, receive, and delivery scope. Attach this extractor only to the intended operation instrumenters, or update the PR's documented telemetry scope if the broader behavior is intentional.
